title: AI Systems Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Menlo Security is the leader in Browser Security for human and agentic workforces. Our mission is to enable humans and agents to connect, communicate, and collaborate securely, without compromise. The Menlo Browser Security Platform protects organizations from cyberattacks by stopping threats across the web, documents, and email before they reach the user. With Menlo Agent Runtime Security (MARS), that protection now extends to the AI agents working alongside every employee. Menlo Security is trusted by major global businesses, including Fortune 500 companies and government agencies, to protect their most valuable asset, their data, and is backed by top-tier investors.

We are seeking an AI Systems Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) to lead the platform and backend architecture powering our real-time security detection services. In this role, you will build and scale low-latency serving infrastructure for Small Language Models (SLM), Prompt Injection (PI) engines, and Content / Intent Classification platforms running across GPU and cloud clusters. We are looking for a strong systems engineer who understands production backend services, microservices, container management, and high-throughput inference optimization. While you will work closely with ML researchers, your primary focus will be engineering robust backend services, GPU replica scaling, guardrails, and automated evaluation infrastructure.

Outcomes & KPIs Key Outcome(s) Owned:

  • Sub-hundred-millisecond SLM and detection service execution speeds across high-volume tenant workloads.

  • Highly resilient, auto-scaling GPU inference cluster infrastructure with automated CI/CD and regression gating.

Success Metrics / KPIs:

  • P95 and P99 detection latency for prompt injection (PI) and classification services.

  • GPU pod readiness time and cluster auto-scaling efficiency under burst traffic.

  • Service availability and rate-limiting guardrail enforcement per tenant.

What You'll Do

  • Architect, build, and optimize production serving pipelines for Small Language Models (SLMs) and traditional ML models using model quantization, batching, and GPU acceleration.

  • Own and scale backend microservices (e.g., sds-service-prompt-injection, sds-service-ddr) delivering real-time threat detection.

  • Build consumption-based monitoring, tenant rate-limiting, and runtime guardrail infrastructure.

  • Manage and optimize GPU cluster replicas (Kubernetes / Pod infrastructure) to minimize cold-start times and manage infrastructure costs.

  • Build continuous evaluation, automated retraining pipelines, model CI/CD, and automated regression gates to test model detection quality against live benchmarks.

  • Refactor legacy service boundaries, service-to-service auth flows, and backend database configurations.

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building distributed backend systems or high-throughput microservices.

  • Proven track record in model serving and inference optimization (e.g., TensorRT, vLLM, ONNX Runtime, Triton Inference Server).

  • Strong programming experience in Python, Go, or C++.

  • Hands-on expertise with Kubernetes, container orchestration, GPU scheduling, and infrastructure auto-scaling.

  • Solid understanding of CI/CD pipelines, MLOps/LLMops principles, and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).

Preferred / Nice to Have:

  • Experience building consumption-based rate limiting or multi-tenant guardrail architectures.

  • Familiarity with database refactoring, auth protocols, and backend technical debt remediation.

  • Background in cybersecurity, threat detection engines, or DLP/PII filtering platforms.

  • Experience benchmarking runtime vs. accuracy trade-offs between local SLMs and cloud LLMs (e.g., Vertex AI).

  • Experience with AWS, GCP, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Linux.

title: AI Systems - Senior Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on our AI Systems team, you'll build the AI foundations and product experiences of Ledgy: the Ledgy Agent, the tools and skills it runs on, our MCP server, and the platform capabilities that let other teams embed AI safely in their domains. You'll collaborate with fellow engineers, product managers, and designers in a new and fast-moving product area where correctness matters as much as speed - our customers need equity data they can trust.

Location: We hire remotely across the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania. For candidates based in London, we use a hybrid model with 2 days in the office per week.

The team you'll join:
AI Systems - Develops Ledgy's AI foundations and product experiences, from AI agents and AI-assisted workflows to the platform capabilities that help other teams embed AI safely in their domains. The team works in a new and evolving product area, balancing rapid iteration with reliable execution, evaluation tooling, and responsible automation.

What You'll Work On

Help build the future of how companies manage equity.

  • Ledgy Agent. You'll design and build the system behind our in-app agent, so equity administrators can do through AI what they do manually in the app today. Ledgy Agent takes real actions and runs real analysis on live equity data, like onboarding a stakeholder end to end, and administrators depend on its accuracy and observability. You'll design the tools, skills, context, and orchestration behind it, and how it decides to handle each request.
  • Ledgy MCP. Not everyone wants to open Ledgy to get things done. Our MCP server lets customers bring equity into the AI agents and tools they already use. You'll shape it alongside the in-app agent, so a capability built once works in both places, and you'll decide what we expose and how we keep it safe.
  • Measuring and improving the agent. You'll design and build the system we use to measure the agent's quality and learn from how customers use it: evaluations, tracing, and feedback from real conversations. You decide what "good" means for customers, how we measure it, and how what we learn changes what we build next.
  • Scaling. The Ledgy web application, the agent, MCP, and surfaces we haven't built yet all need the same capabilities. You'll design the foundations that let us build AI features once and reuse them everywhere, and that let other teams add AI to their domains without compromising correctness. You'll also design how it runs as usage grows: the backend infrastructure, cost, and latency behind the agent and MCP, and how we keep them reliable and observable.

You'll own real parts of this and have a say in where we invest. You'll also spend time with customers to see how administrators actually use the agent, and use that to decide what to build next.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. These are the things that would make you an especially good fit.

  • You have 5+ years of experience working as a Software Engineer, with strong TypeScript/Node fundamentals across back end and front end
  • You've built and shipped agentic or LLM-based software to production, such as an agent, an assistant, or a chat product, and you've been the one running it. You've debugged failures in real conversations and kept cost and latency in check as usage and models changed.
  • You've designed the agent itself: tools and skills, context and prompt engineering, state, streaming, and the agent loop. You know at least one agent framework or runtime well and can say where it works and where it doesn't.
  • You improve these systems with evidence. Evals, regression sets, tracing, and feedback from real usage tell you whether a change helped, and you use them to decide what to do next.
  • You keep up with what the foundation labs and the wider community are learning about building agents. You try new techniques early and judge which ones make our product better and are worth adopting now, and which should wait.
  • You take part in deciding what we build. You read the data, talk to customers, and push for what you think matters most.

Our Tech Stack

We work in a TypeScript monorepo: React and Tailwind on the front end, tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, and Temporal on the back end. It runs on GCP with Kubernetes, managed through Terraform. The agent is currently built on the Vercel AI SDK, and we run an MCP server alongside it.

You don't need to know all of it, but hands-on experience building with LLMs is strongly preferred.

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First day: Get the app running locally and make your first commit. Your onboarding buddy helps you get there.

First week:

  • Meet the engineers, product managers, and designers you'll work with.
  • Learn the agent end to end: its tools, skills, MCP surface, and how we evaluate it.
  • Ship a few smaller features.

First month:

  • Meet the wider engineering team and learn how Ledgy works and how customers use it today. This is the background you'll use for decisions later.
  • Make larger contributions and take a bigger part in code reviews.

First 3 months:

  • Drive part of a larger piece of work, such as process, tooling, a new product, or new functionality.
  • Work with Product and Design to prove and deepen the value AI adds to the product.
  • Take part in architecture and long-term decisions.

After the first 3 months:

  • Take a bigger role in shaping where the team is heading. Own key parts of our AI platform and decide where we can add the most value for customers.
  • Mentor other engineers and raise the bar. Help teams across Ledgy add AI to what they build, whether that means advising, reviewing, or working alongside them.
  • Help shape Ledgy's technical direction, for AI and for everything else we build.

The interview process:

  • Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role
  • Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.
  • System Design (60 min): A system design session where you will design an architecture for a problem from the Ledgy domain using a visual tool of your choice
  • Behavioural (45 min): Answer behavioural style questions about your experience, using the STAR method - with a PM and EM.
  • Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy's mission and values
  • Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means:

  • Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.
  • We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.
  • This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.
  • For candidates based in London we use a hybrid work model of 2 days in the office per week.

title: AI Transformation Lead
descriptionHtml:

Who we are

Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent, and we're building our Berlin hub to serve clients across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

Why now

We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them; the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it.

As an AI Transformation Lead in Berlin, you’ll work on our most ambitious client engagements across DACH, helping leading businesses redefine themselves through AI. You’ll own major workstreams alongside a Senior AI Transformation Lead and the AI engineers who build with you. You’ll map how a business runs its key processes, find where AI fundamentally changes the economics, and redesign them agentic-first rather than bolting AI onto today’s process. You’ll prototype the new workflows yourself with Claude Code or similar, build the analysis behind the business case, and track the productivity or revenue each build delivers once it’s live. What we’re looking for: You have extreme agency, operate with urgency, and have consistently been among the top performers wherever you’ve been, at university or at work. You’re a builder with a deep understanding of technology. You don’t need to write production code, but you use AI every day, build with it yourself (prototype workflows, agents, internal tools), know what models can and can’t do, and hold your own with engineers. You’re as comfortable with a client’s managers as with the operators doing the work. PE portfolio or value creation experience, exposure to software or services businesses, and German for client work in DACH are a plus. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway.

What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Frontier AI work with real stakes, driving tangible outcomes for consequential companies. Learning from people who have embedded AI into 50+ businesses, with scope that grows as fast as your impact. A team built to be one of the most talent-dense in Europe, and the chance to shape how the firm delivers and grows in Berlin as an early joiner. A chance to help close Europe’s AI gap, moving European businesses to the right side of the productivity chasm.

Logistics: Berlin, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in DACH and Europe. English is our working language; German is a plus. We can sponsor visas for eligible candidates, and start dates are flexible.

Apply

Send your CV and a short note on a problem you're proudest of solving and the impact it had.

We hire people from every background and judge them on what they've built. If you don't tick every box, apply anyway.

Resonance is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need adjustments at any stage, tell us and we'll make them.

title: AIT Systems Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.

You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.

The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.

Responsibilities

Functional and system testing

  • Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.

  • Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.

  • Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.

  • Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.

  • Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.

  • Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.

Verification tracking

  • Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.

  • Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.

  • Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.

  • Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.

GSE and test infrastructure

  • Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.

  • Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.

  • Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.

Integration and campaign support

  • Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.

  • Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.

  • Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.

  • Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.

Requirements

  • Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.

  • Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.

  • Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.

  • Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.

  • Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.

  • Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.

  • Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.

  • Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.

  • Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).

  • Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.

Desirables

  • End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.

  • Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).

  • Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).

  • Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.

  • Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).

  • Launch campaign experience at a launch site.

  • Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.

  • Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.

Personal attributes

  • Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.

  • Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.

  • Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.

  • Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.

  • Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

  • Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

Send us your CV in English or German. No formal cover letter is needed. A GitHub link or an app you have worked on is welcome, but optional.

title: Applied AI Scientist, Simulation & Reinforcement Learning
descriptionHtml:
At Locus Robotics, we build AI-powered systems and intelligent robots that keep global supply chains running. Our platform combines advanced AI, real-time decision-making, and autonomous robotics to help leading companies improve efficiency, scale operations, and adapt to constant change.

Locus Robotics is a place to do meaningful work with real-world impact, where your ideas move quickly from concept to deployment. We invest in our people, encourage continuous learning, and give you the opportunity to grow your career while building technology that is used every day at global scale.

As an Applied AI Scientist, Simulation & Reinforcement Learning, you'll own the simulator behind SDL, our programme building a world-first, reinforcement-learning-driven orchestration framework for people and robots. That framework needs a simulator that is trustworthy enough to develop, tune and validate it before it touches a live warehouse.

You will take over day-to-day ownership of our discrete-event simulation (built on SimPy), make it measurably closer to reality, and use it as the training and evaluation ground for learning-based policies. Simulation comes first; reinforcement learning grows to be the larger part of the role as the simulator matures. You'll compare your simulations against live operational data from some of the world's largest fulfilment sites, and your work will decide what is validated and shipped to fleets of robots in customer sites worldwide.

This is not a notebook role. The simulator you own is the foundation that decides what ships to customer sites worldwide. You will work in a small, collaborative team where research meets production, as part of Applied Data Science (ADS), reporting to Oscar Mendez.

  • Location: This is a remote position based in the United Kingdom. Candidates must reside in the UK. Right to Work: Candidates must have the legal right to work in the UK. Locus Robotics is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position, now or in the future.

Responsibilities

Own the simulator

  • Own and develop our SimPy-based discrete-event simulator, including its logic, design choices and the fragile areas that need care.
  • Pay down technical debt: improve test coverage, code quality, reproducibility and developer tooling.
  • Build the experiment infrastructure around the simulator: orchestration, study management, reporting and automated runs across benchmark sites.
  • Generate and maintain site data (e.g. distance files, configs) needed to simulate customer warehouses.
  • Support scenario testing and sensitivity analysis for our order-engine and orchestration teams.

Tune and close the sim2real gap

  • Define, measure and reduce the sim-to-real gap against real site data.
  • Run parameter optimisation and tuning studies (e.g. Optuna), and diagnose anomalies and non-determinism.
  • Model warehouse processes such as congestion, picker behaviour and queueing at the right level of fidelity.
  • Communicate results and confidence clearly to engineering, product and operations stakeholders.
  • Use Optimization, RL & DL to tune the simulator

Grow into reinforcement learning

  • Turn the simulator into a proper RL environment (Gymnasium/Gym-style interfaces) with fast, repeatable, scalable training runs.
  • Design, train and evaluate RL policies, starting with guidance generation, and benchmark them against current heuristic algorithms.
  • Guard against overfitting to simulator artefacts, and design experiments that show what transfers to the real world.
  • Prototype, evaluate and productionise learning-based components alongside the wider ML, MLOps and OE teams.
  • Stay current with RL, multi-agent systems and simulation research, and assess what is applicable to Locus.
  • Contribute to internal technical papers, patents and, where appropriate, publications.

Qualifications

  • A PhD in Computer Science, AI/ML, Robotics, Mathematics, Physics, Operations Research or a related quantitative field, or MSc and 5+ years of industry experience applying AI/ML or simulation to real-world problems.
  • Hands-on experience building, extending or validating simulators, ideally discrete-event simulation (SimPy or similar).
  • Practical experience with reinforcement learning and training simulation-based agents, including simulation for RL and Gym-style environments.
  • Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals: testing, code review, maintainable and reproducible code.
  • Rigorous experimental and statistical thinking: benchmarking, tuning, ablations, uncertainty.
  • Experience in robotics, logistics, warehouse or other operations-heavy domains.
  • Publications in major AI, ML, robotics or vision venues (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV).
  • Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to engage diverse audiences effectively and explain uncertain results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences in a multidisciplinary environment.

The expected base salary range for this role is GBP 70,000 - 120,000 based on external market data, plus bonus and equity. Actual offers will depend on factors such as the candidate's experience, education, training, key or critical skills, geographic location, and current market and business conditions.

Additional Information 

Locus Robotics is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Associate
descriptionHtml:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

 

About the team

 

Our Energy, Transition and Environment business unit is pioneering meaningful change in the clean energy revolution. Our vision is to accelerate the transition to net-zero emissions and drive efficiencies for a new era of utility companies.

 

We believe that the responsible, and intelligent, deployment of AI is critical to the success of this mission. We partner with a wide range of clients - from major energy operators, to GreenTech startups, and national infrastructure providers - to build solutions which return measurable impact and move us towards a smarter, cleaner, and more sustainable world.

 


About the role

 

As an Associate, you’ll be part of a close-knit team - scoping, building and delivering impactful AI projects for our clients in the industry.

We’ll look to you to build trusted client relationships, analyse requirements and feedback, stay on top of workflows and help to ensure our bespoke AI tools are optimised for real-world operations.

This is an exciting, new role for an individual motivated to build their knowledge of AI transformation in the Energy value chain.

  

What you'll be doing

 

  • Managing individual work streams to support the successful delivery and implementation of bespoke AI solutions

  • Working side-by-side with Government stakeholders to understand critical mission challenges and user needs

  • Conducting open-source analysis to support the development of cutting-edge AI tools

  • Translating complex operational requirements into clear user stories for delivery and engineering teams.

  • Designing and testing workflows that support user-centric decision-making in high-stakes environments

  • Collaborating closely with technical teams to ensure projects run smoothly and solutions meet customer needs

  • Contributing to internal thought leadership, strategy, and capability development across the team

     

Who we're looking for

 

  • You demonstrate analytical thinking, can clearly communicate ideas, and synthesise complex information

  • You have some experience working on AI/data intensive projects in the Energy sector

  • You have external client-facing experience and have built trusted relationships which have contributed to the overall success of projects/products

  • You’ve worked with technical teams

  • You understand Agile and related methodologies and the basis of iterative development and continuous delivery

  • You are thoughtful and proactive in ambiguous situations, with examples of when you’ve taken initiative and owned finding solutions to challenges

  • You’re excited and knowledgeable about the possibilities for innovation in Government technology

  

Our interview process

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 mins)

  2. Introduction Interview (60 mins)

  3. Case Study Interview (60 mins)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Simulation & Robotics, 2027 (Zurich)
descriptionHtml:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the Role:

The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry.

As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products.

If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you.

 

Areas of Responsibility:

  • Core Simulator Architecture: Design, implement, and evolve the foundational architecture of the Skydio Simulator, ensuring it scales across vehicle types, environments, and use cases.

  • Physics and Dynamics: Improve and extend physics models governing vehicle motion, interactions with the environment, and dynamic agents.

  • Sensor and Hardware Simulation: Build high-fidelity simulations of cameras, IMUs, and other onboard components, including timing, noise characteristics, and hardware behavior.

  • Autonomy Stack Integration: Run and validate the full Skydio autonomy stack in simulation, ensuring consistency between simulated and real-world behavior.

  • Feature Development on Top of the Core: Implement simulator capabilities that unlock new workflows for customers and internal autonomy engineers, from training scenarios to advanced testing modes.

  • Performance and Fidelity: Profile, optimize, and improve simulator performance while continuously pushing realism and accuracy.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop core simulator components in C++ and Python, working close to real-time constraints.

  • Collaborate with autonomy, perception, and controls engineers to align simulation behavior with real-world systems.

  • Debug complex interactions between physics, sensors, autonomy logic, and rendering.

  • Help shape the long-term technical direction of the simulator as both a product and an internal platform.

  • Contribute to documentation and shared understanding of how the simulator works internally.

Qualifications:

  • Strong software engineering experience with C++ and Python.

  • Experience building complex systems where performance, determinism, or correctness matter.

  • Comfort reasoning about time-synchronized systems, state machines, or real-time execution.

  • Ability to work in a large, evolving codebase with multiple stakeholders.

  • Interest in robotics, simulation, or physical systems (prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement).

Bonus Experience:

  • Robotics, simulation, game engines, or real-time systems.

  • Physics engines, sensor modeling, or hardware abstraction layers.

  • Multithreaded or low-latency system design.

  • Experience debugging systems that span software and physical behavior.

Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends.

*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position's location.

title: Brand Designer, Web
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR — We're seeking an exceptional Brand Designer to own the visual direction and craft of our website. You'll shape how Lovable looks, feels and communicates online - working closely with design engineering and marketing to turn ideas into world-class web experiences.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.


What we're looking for

  • 7+ years of experience, with a portfolio of shipped websites that demonstrate strong visual craft and brand thinking

  • Portfolio showing landing pages, brand systems, or marketing sites where design decisions clearly serve the story (if your portfolio is mostly product/UI work - check out our other roles)

  • A sharp eye for typography, layout, color, and motion, with the taste to know what's on-brand and what isn't

  • Comfort designing directly for the web - you think in real breakpoints, real type scales, and real constraints, not just static comps

  • Ability to systematise creative choices in design systems - contributing to a shared design system across both product and brand

  • Experience partnering closely with design engineers to get explorations into production without losing the soul of the idea

  • You’re no stranger to shipping your own designs directly to production - perhaps with a little help from AI

  • Ideally - you've got a point of view on where web design is headed and aren't afraid to push for something unexpected

  • We’re prioritising candidates based in London or Stockholm, or willing to relocate


What you'll do

In one sentence: Own the visual and brand craft of Lovable's website, making sure every page feels unmistakably Lovable.

  • Design landing pages, campaign sites, and web experiences that make people stop scrolling

  • Set and evolve the visual language for lovable.dev - typography, layout systems, imagery, motion principles

  • Pair closely with design engineering to translate explorations into scalable, web-native implementations, staying involved through to shipped pixels

  • Collaborate with marketing and brand to make sure the website tells the right story at the right moment - launches, campaigns, positioning shifts

  • Build and maintain a visual system that keeps the site consistent while leaving room for creative surprises

  • Bring a strong opinion on craft and hold the line on quality, even under deadline pressure

  • Help define what "world-class" looks like for marketing sites

How we hire

  1. Fill in a short form then jump on an intro call with a recruiter.

  2. Show us some of your work you're really proud of.

  3. Walk us through your process and craft across several design interviews.

  4. In some cases, we may opt to do paid, trial work.

About your application

  • Please submit your application in English — it's our company language so you'll be speaking lots of it if you join

  • We treat all candidates equally — if you're interested please apply through our careers portal

title: Build Your Own Internship – m/f/d (min. 6 Months)
descriptionHtml:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe’s largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

 

About the Role

This is a full-time internship of at least 6 months at our Berlin HQ, and it is not a regular internship application. We don’t want your CV first. We want to see what you have built.

If you build with AI because you can’t stop, with Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or anything else, show us. If your project convinces us, we shape the internship around you and your strengths.

 

What We Want to See

Record a Loom of something you built with AI. It should be no longer than 5 minutes. Two kinds of projects get our attention:

  • Something that would help Langdock. Look at our product roadmap and at our product, and build something that solves a real problem for us or our customers. That could be a feature prototype, an internal tool, a GTM engine, a support automation, an eval setup, or something we haven’t thought of yet.

  • A genuine passion project. Something you built because you couldn’t stop thinking about it, and that shows how you think.

What we don’t want: basic chatbots, simple prompt wrappers, “summarize my inbox” agents, or linear three-step workflows. Our customers build those every day. Show us something that made you think hard, and that makes us think too.

 

What Your Loom Should Cover

  • The problem: what you solved and why it matters.

  • The demo: show it working live, not on slides.

  • How it’s built: the models, tools, architecture, and key decisions behind it.

  • What broke: where it failed and what you learned from that.

  • What’s next: what you would build at Langdock if you joined.

 

What You Will Do

  • Own a real project. Ideally it’s the one you showed us. You take it from prototype to something our team or customers actually use.

  • Work directly with the team. You work alongside Product, Engineering, or GTM, depending on where your project lives.

  • Ship, measure, iterate. You present your progress regularly and decide based on real feedback.

 

How to Apply

Paste your Loom URL into the field “Your Build” in the application form. Your LinkedIn profile is enough; a CV is optional.

 

You Might Be a Fit If…

  • You build, not just talk about AI. You have shipped things that work, even if they’re rough.

  • You think in impact, not just in technology.

  • You show high agency. You don’t wait for tasks; you find them.

  • You experiment constantly with new models and tools.

  • You communicate clearly and professionally in English. German is a plus.

  • You are kind and care about the people around you.

 

What We Need

  • Availability for a full-time internship of at least 6 months, 100% on-site in Berlin.

  • A work permit for Germany.

 

The Environment

You will work from our Berlin office at Greifswalder Straße 212, where all of us work together in person, surrounded by people building AI products and infrastructure every day. Lunch and dinner are catered in the office. We look after ourselves, and gym membership and coaching resources are part of the standard package. We value Calm Urgency, Ambitious Execution, and Caring Ownership. The vibe is calm but intense.

 

Next Steps

We move fast. If you have built something you’re proud of, show us.

Du übernimmst die fachliche und disziplinarische Führung eines Teams von Business Development Representatives und entwickelst dieses zu einer leistungsstarken Outbound-Organisation weiter.

Wir suchen eine Person mit einem starken operativen Sales-Background und erster bzw. fundierter Führungserfahrung in einem ambitionierten B2B-Vertriebsumfeld.

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Business Development / Sales Development / Outbound Sales

Die Position bietet deutlich mehr Gestaltungsspielraum als eine klassische Team-Lead-Rolle.

Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Launched in May 2026 with Mobilize Financial Services (Renault, Nissan, Dacia, and Alpine), our platform allows end-of-lease drivers to profile cars directly through our app and auction them to 8,000+ verified dealers. As the department’s first dedicated commercial hire, you will build this business line from the ground up and shape a high-growth product inside an established scale-up. You will serve as the day-to-day contact for enterprise partners, running business reviews, tracking performance, and fully owning key relationships within six months. Acting as the operational bridge between external partners, our dealer network, and internal product, engineering, and ops teams, you will troubleshoot issues, write scalable runbooks, and collaborate with the commercial lead on pitches and new client onboarding.

What you’ll be doing:

What you’ll do:

  • Drive commercial strategy: Identify growth opportunities across partner, dealer, and transport revenue streams, collaborating closely with partner Commercial Leads to optimise pricing and fee structures.

  • Lead key partnerships: Serve as the trusted, day-to-day contact for Enterprise partners - leading monthly and quarterly business reviews backed by robust data and actionable insights.

title: Certification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About EH Energy Engineering

EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

Key responsibilities

Certification strategy and project management

  • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

  • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

  • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

Safety engineering and risk analysis

  • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

  • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

  • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

  • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

Compliance and technical documentation

  • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

  • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

  • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

  • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

Collaboration and continuous improvement

  • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

  • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

Standards and regulatory scope

The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

  • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

Required qualifications

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

  • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

  • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

  • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

  • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

  • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

  • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

  • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

Preferred qualifications and personal profile

Nice to have

  • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

  • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

  • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

  • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

Personal profile

  • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

  • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

  • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

  • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

Start date: Immediately

title: Commercial Operations Associate
descriptionHtml:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

Griffin is a UK bank built for builders. We give fintechs and platforms the bank accounts and payment rails to launch their own financial products, and clients like Uber, Yonder, Anna Money and Counting Up build on us. Our commercial team brings sales, customer success and marketing together to win, onboard and grow those clients. We’re a team of 10 people, made up of former founders and growth specialists.

The opportunity

You’ll become the engine behind how our commercial team makes decisions. Working alongside the Chief Revenue Officer, the Head of Commercial and the Head of Marketing, you’ll see the full picture of how a bank wins, onboards and grows its clients, and your analysis will shape where the team focuses next. There’s no narrow lane here. One week you’re building a forecast, the next you’re preparing a renewal review, and if something needs an owner, it’s yours.

What success looks like

In your first 6 months, you’ll have given the commercial team a forecast it trusts and spotted risks early, so every quarter end runs smoothly. People across Sales, Customer Success and Marketing will rely on our data because it’s accurate and up to date, and the team’s reviews will run like clockwork. The board and investors will receive numbers they can follow with confidence, and the executive team will already be turning to you for its priority projects.

To do this you’ll own

  • The numbers: the reporting that runs our commercial business, from pipeline and bookings to annual recurring revenue (ARR), net revenue retention and consumption against forecast, plus pricing and deal-structure modelling, including consumption-based pricing and customer profitability

  • Our CRM: clean, well-structured data, built with Sales and Customer Success around clear stage definitions and fields people actually use

  • Sales and customer success insight: analysis of conversion, sales cycle length, win and loss reasons and pipeline coverage, plus account analysis for renewals covering volumes, revenue, margin and product adoption

  • Marketing performance: campaign tracking and pipeline attribution so every pound of spend ties back to revenue, alongside ad hoc work like target account lists and event reporting

  • Commercial governance: deal approval and discount policies, pricing and contract records and clear audit trails, working with Legal, Compliance and Finance

  • Our operating cadence: documented processes and the weekly, monthly and quarterly reviews that keep the team in rhythm

  • Executive projects: high-priority projects, briefings and materials that give you close exposure to how strategic decisions get made

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that’s for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To ensure this, we’re looking for people who have most of the following:

  • You’ll have some experience as an operator. If it’s in a commercial, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, consulting or finance role then that’s a bonus

  • A habit of rolling up your sleeves and taking ownership without waiting to be asked

  • Curiosity about fintech, banking and how money moves

  • A structured mind and an eye for detail, with the flexibility to switch between spreadsheets, research and talking to people, and a knack for finding the story in the numbers and explaining it simply

  • The ability to learn quickly, ask good questions and take feedback well

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have experience in fintech, SaaS or a fast-growing startup

  • Want to build a career in commercial, sales or growth

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

What We’re Looking For

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

  • CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

title: Corporate Account Executive
descriptionHtml:
Overview 

As a Corporate Account Executive, you will own new-logo ARR growth across private-sector organisations with 2,000–7,499 employees in the UK, Ireland and South Africa. This is a pure acquisition and self-sourcing role with no inherited customer base or ongoing account-management responsibility. While you will have access to BDR, Solution Engineering, Partner Account Management and Marketing support, you remain personally accountable for building sufficient pipeline, creating your own qualified opportunities and achieving the ARR target. Once fully ramped, the role will carry an annual net-new ARR quota in the region of US $900,000.

What will you be doing? 

You will build, own and execute a territory and pipeline-generation plan that creates sustainable pipeline and converts opportunities into net-new ARR. The territory is not verticalized, so you will use available account intelligence, SKU performance, industry growth and market data to determine where to focus. You will personally self-source qualified opportunities while using internal and partner resources to extend your reach and accelerate results. You will manage the full sales cycle, from account prioritisation and prospecting through discovery, solution alignment, commercial negotiation and close.

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Building, owning and executing a data-led territory and pipeline-generation plan that explains how you will achieve your net-new ARR quota, where you will focus, how you will personally create qualified opportunities and which resources you will engage.
  • Generating business exclusively through new-logo acquisition across the defined private-sector segment; the role will not inherit existing customers.
  • Using account, industry, SKU-growth and market data to prioritise opportunities and continually refine your territory strategy.
  • Personally self-sourcing qualified opportunities through disciplined prospecting and account development, while effectively using BDR, Marketing and partner resources to complement—not replace—your own pipeline creation. Building pipeline through a balanced combination of self-sourced activity, BDR support, marketing programmes and partner-led engagement.
  • Working closely with the Partner Account Manager to identify the right partners, develop joint account plans, create pipeline and progress opportunities. As a channel-first organisation, effective partner engagement is fundamental to success in this role.
  • Leading consultative, value-based sales cycles across business, technical and executive stakeholders, positioning a platform outcome rather than relying on a single-product sale.
  • Partnering with Solution Engineering to shape discovery, demonstrate relevant capabilities and build credible business and technical solutions.
  • Planning and delivering compelling presentations, proposals and business cases that connect customer challenges to measurable outcomes, value and return on investment.
  • Maintaining strong deal control throughout complex sales cycles, including stakeholder mapping, qualification, mutual action planning, commercial negotiation and accurate forecasting.
  • Maintaining complete, accurate and current account, opportunity, pipeline and forecast information in the CRM system.
  • Attending customer and partner meetings remotely and in person across the territory; this is a field-based role in which face-to-face collaboration is expected.
  • Coordinating with Customer Success when a new customer reaches the applicable ARR threshold, ensuring an effective transition and appropriate post-sale engagement.

The Team Behind Your Territory

You will retain clear ownership of the territory plan, pipeline creation and ARR result while working as part of a collaborative go-to-market team. The supporting teams provide expertise, reach and leverage, but do not replace the Account Executive’s responsibility to self-source opportunities and create sufficient pipeline. Support available includes:

  • Business Development Representative: support with targeted prospecting, account engagement and meeting creation.
  • Solution Engineer: technical discovery, demonstrations, solution design and technical validation.
  • Partner Account Manager: partner strategy, account alignment, introductions, joint pipeline creation and channel-led deal execution.
  • Marketing: campaigns, events, content, intent signals and account-based support.
  • Customer Success: post-sale engagement for customers that meet the applicable ARR threshold.

Is this the role for you?

We are looking for an entrepreneurial, commercially focused sales professional who is comfortable creating a market rather than inheriting one. You will be confident making evidence-based choices about where to invest your time, mobilising internal and partner resources, and remaining accountable for the execution of your plan and the ARR outcome.

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • A strong track record of winning net-new business and meeting or exceeding ARR or ACV-based quotas in a complex B2B sales environment.
  • Experience managing full-cycle software or technology sales into medium-to-large private-sector organisations.
  • Demonstrated ability to build productive channel relationships and create and close partner-led opportunities in a channel-first model.
  • Experience developing and executing territory and account plans using market, industry, product and account data, with a proven ability to self-source qualified pipeline.
  • Confidence selling to business, technical and executive stakeholders and translating complex requirements into clear commercial value.
  • Strong pipeline creation, qualification, forecasting, negotiation and closing discipline.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, listening and stakeholder-management skills.
  • The initiative, resilience and accountability to operate independently while bringing the right cross-functional resources together.

A collaborative, curious and adaptable approach, with the willingness to test new ideas and continuously improve.

title: Customer Director
descriptionHtml:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the role

As a Customer Director at Faculty, you will spearhead ambitious growth across our Public Services portfolio. Blending strategic consulting with AI delivery, you will unlock potential for UK Government departments and international partners.

You will lead multi-disciplinary teams to design AI solutions, navigate multi-million-pound programmes, and build trusting relationships with senior government stakeholders across key areas like the Home Office, Department for Education, DWP, HMRC, DEFRA, and MHCLG.

This is an entrepreneurial opportunity to shape the future of public services by turning cutting-edge AI into operational impact.

What you'll be doing:

  • Driving sales growth and executing strategic account plans to hit ambitious multi-million-pound revenue targets across central government accounts.

  • Leading complex commercial negotiations, bidding opportunities, and pricing proposals for new and existing public sector portfolios.

  • Nurturing long-term relationships with senior government budget holders and C-suite stakeholders to ensure high client satisfaction.

  • Overseeing cross-functional delivery teams to guarantee high-quality execution of large-scale AI transformation programmes and GDS-style digital products and the associated digital service and technology infrastructure required

  • Mentoring team members to accelerate their professional development while supporting scalable business unit growth.

  • Proactively identifying innovative, data-oriented AI use cases that solve complex public sector challenges.

  • Advising client directors on AI strategy, engineering concepts, and technical implementation to demonstrate continuous value.

  • Serving as a key member of the Public Services leadership group, shaping strategic direction, driving commercial growth, and embedding customer excellence across the sector.

Who we're looking for:

  • You bring a comprehensive background in consulting or public sector strategy, with proven experience leading large-scale transformation programmes across government and public accounts.

  • You possess a natural business development mindset, combining an appetite for commercial hunting with deep relationship-building skills to manage multi-million-pound deal processes.

  • You bring demonstrable experience in digital government transformation alongside strong commercial fluency in cutting-edge AI capabilities.

  • You excel at managing complex stakeholder relationships, guiding senior civil servants through fast-paced, high-stakes programmes with structured problem-solving.

  • You bring technical curiosity and acumen to engage confidently with technical teams and advise client directors on AI and advise client directors on the creative and safe applications of AI within their most important areas of business.

  • You demonstrate an entrepreneurial, adaptable leadership style with a proven ability to translate intricate technical concepts into real business value.

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

  2. Introduction to Hiring Manager (60 minutes)

  3. Discovery Role Play Interview (60 minutes)

  4. Commercial & Leadership Interview (60 minutes)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

What you'll do

  • Handle security questionnaires end to end: intake, drafting, review, and delivery for customer security assessments, RFPs, and vendor evaluations, in whatever format they arrive (OneTrust, spreadsheets, portals, email), pulling in Security, Legal, or Engineering when an answer needs it.

  • Operate our trust automation platform: use and help improve the system that generates answers from our governed knowledge base. Review output for accuracy, flag weak or incorrect answers, and help keep the guardrails from over-claiming.

  • Keep the knowledge base current: update answers as the platform, certifications, and control environment change; ingest new evidence (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701/42001, HIPAA, penetration tests); and flag stale facts before they reach a customer.

  • Handle one-off customer requests: evidence requests, Trust Center access, point questions from account teams, and anything that doesn't fit a questionnaire but still shapes a customer's confidence.

  • Support customer calls: join prospect and customer calls alongside Sales and Solutions to field security, privacy, and AI-safety questions, especially for UK and EMEA customers. Partner with the sales team from intake through close.

  • Support contract reviews: work with Legal and Deal Desk on security and privacy terms in DPAs and MSAs, including UK GDPR and EU data-transfer questions; learn which positions are standard and which need escalation.

  • Keep the program honest: follow the standing rules that protect us and our customers: state only our standard position, never reference another customer's ask or situation, and escalate anything that needs Legal, Security, or Engineering sign-off.

  • Track program data: log knowledge-base gaps, recurring questions we can't answer well yet, and where automation is saving or costing time, and share findings with the team.

  • Help maintain public trust artifacts: keep the Trust Center, security whitepapers, and supporting evidence current and aligned with what we actually do.

How the role will grow

As you build context on our platform and customers, you'll take on more ownership:

  • Broader program ownership: lead specific parts of the program, such as a framework area, a slice of the knowledge base, or EMEA customer coverage.

  • AI-assurance coverage: help extend the knowledge base to emerging standards like ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, and the EU AI Act.

  • Cross-functional influence: work more closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, and Sales to make our security and AI-safety posture a differentiator rather than a checkbox.

What we're looking for

  • 3 to 5 years of experience in customer-facing security, trust, or GRC roles: security assurance, customer trust, vendor security review, security-focused sales engineering, or similar.

  • Hands-on experience with security questionnaires and the customer security-review process across formats (CAIQ, SIG, custom spreadsheets, OneTrust and similar portals) and frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR/UK GDPR, NIST).

  • Some exposure to contracts (DPAs, MSAs) and the ability to connect contract language to a company's actual security controls.

  • Strong written communication; you can turn a control requirement into a clear, accurate answer, and you know the difference between answering a question and over-answering it.

  • Working knowledge of cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and SaaS architectures; comfortable discussing encryption, isolation, and data flows with technical buyers.

  • Interest in trust automation and AI-assisted tooling, with an understanding that automation needs guardrails.

  • A precise, detail-oriented mindset; you catch the answer that is almost right, and you treat a customer-facing representation as something that has to be true.

  • A collaborative, low-ego approach, and good judgment about when to escalate rather than answer.

  • Comfortable working with a US-based team, including some overlap with US Eastern hours.

  • Bonus: familiarity with AI/ML platforms, LLM inference, or AI governance concepts (zero data retention, content guardrails, EU AI Act).

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.
