Vogel ist inhabergeführt, und du arbeitest unmittelbar an den Themen der Geschäftsführung mit.

Du studierst im fortgeschrittenen Bachelor oder im Master oder bist im Gap Year. Die Fachrichtung ist zweitrangig, wichtig ist, dass du herausgestochen bist. Du willst kein Traineeprogramm mit festen Stationen, sondern wissen, wie Entscheidungen tatsächlich entstehen: mit unvollständigen Daten, unter Zeitdruck, zwischen Menschen unterschiedlicher Meinung.

Das Praktikum dauert drei bis sechs Monate in Vollzeit. Du verantwortest ein bis zwei eigene Themen und arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung.

Deine Verantwortung

Analyse und Entscheidungsvorlagen

  • Du nimmst eine offene Frage der Geschäftsführung, strukturierst sie und lieferst eine Antwort auf zwei Seiten, mit eigener Einschätzung. Dein Maßstab: Wer die Vorlage liest, kann danach entscheiden.

  • Du baust Auswertungen aus unseren Zahlen: Ergebnisse je Einheit, Mandatsstrukturen, Auslastung, Wachstumstreiber. Die Daten holst du selbst, deine Annahmen dokumentierst du mit.

  • Du prüfst Annahmen nach, die im Haus als gesetzt gelten, und stellst sachlich fest, wenn etwas nicht mehr stimmt.

Eigene Themen von der Frage bis zum Ergebnis

  • Du übernimmst eigene Themen über die gesamte Strecke und trägst die Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

  • Du arbeitest in laufenden Vorhaben quer durch das Unternehmen mit: Integration eines zugekauften Hauses, Aufbau eines neuen Beratungsfelds, Einführung eines Werkzeugs in allen Einheiten.

Interne Steuerung und Kultur

  • Du baust an den Formaten mit, über die das Unternehmen gesteuert wird: Berichtswege, Kennzahlen, Entscheidungsvorlagen, interne Kommunikation.

  • Du verantwortest Anlässe, an denen unsere Kultur konkret wird, von der Town Hall bis zum Sommerfest, gemeinsam mit dem Growth-Team.

  • Du wirkst im Recruiting mit: Sichtung, eigene Einschätzung zu Kandidaten, Mitarbeit am Bewerbungsprozess.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 3 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast zwei eigene Themen von der Fragestellung bis zum Ergebnis verantwortet und selbst vorgetragen.

  • Mehrere deiner Entscheidungsvorlagen haben zu tatsächlichen Entscheidungen geführt.

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Die Bereichsleitungen sprechen dich direkt an, wenn sie eine Analyse brauchen.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Du siehst in wenigen Monaten, wie ein wachsendes Unternehmen entscheidet, und nimmst eine Arbeitsweise mit, die in jeder späteren Rolle trägt. Wer überzeugt, bleibt im Gespräch.

Das bringst du mit

  • Erste Praxis in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld ist ein Plus: Beratung, Investment Banking, Private Equity, Scale-up, Founders Office oder eine eigene Gründung.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Denkschärfe und Umsetzungskraft mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du schreibst klar und knapp. Zwei gute Seiten schlagen bei uns zwanzig vollständige.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Analyse und Drafting. Repetitive Aufgaben sind für dich ein Anlass zur Automatisierung.

  • Bei einer offen formulierten Aufgabe machst du deine Annahmen explizit, schlägst eine Richtung ein und justierst unterwegs.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du verträgst die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung: schnelle Iteration, hohe Eigenständigkeit und auch Aufgaben, die nicht im Lebenslauf glänzen.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Die Steuerberaterin mit 20 Jahren Erfahrung weiß Dinge über ihr Mandat, die in keinem Modell stehen.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keine Konzern-Strategieabteilung. Was du schreibst, geht in eine Entscheidung, die diese Woche fällt.

  • Keinen Elfenbeinturm. Eine Empfehlung ohne Verantwortung für die Umsetzung ist hier keine Lieferung.

  • Kein Praktikum mit Rotationsplan. Du bekommst eigene Themen und damit auch die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen.

  • Keine Zuarbeit für eine Zwischenebene. Du trägst deine Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

title: Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
About Grubel

Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window.

To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands.

Grubel was founded in 2026 by Moritz Hardt, director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and formerly a UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher; and Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning at the Technical University of Munich, on leave to build Grubel. The founding team includes engineers with PhDs in computer science and experience in foundation-model pretraining at Mistral and legal AI research at Thomson Reuters. The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen.

Point Nine led an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round with backing from leading AI researchers and founders, including Jeff Dean, Chris Ré, Ion Stoica, and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg.


About the role

We are looking for a Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist to develop the methods and systems that make matter-specific AI possible. You will work on data curation, agent environment design, model adaptation, training, and evaluation. We do not draw a sharp boundary between research and engineering: everyone contributes substantial code, owns experiments end-to-end, builds systems, and helps turn successful methods into products. Research is empirical and engineering intensive.

You will work directly with Grubel’s founders, engineers, legal experts, and enterprise partners. As an early member of the team, you will also help shape Grubel’s technical direction and research culture.

What you’ll work on

  • Developing, testing, and evaluating methods for adapting models and agents to individual legal matters

  • Designing benchmarks and evaluation tasks for complex legal capabilities

  • Developing data curation strategies for scaling from evaluation tasks to training tasks

  • Building infrastructure for training, inference, experimentation, and evaluation

  • Working with legal experts and enterprise partners to turn legal workflows into agentic workflows

  • Turning successful research methods into reliable product capabilities

You may be a good fit if

  • You hold a master’s degree or PhD in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or a related field, or have equivalent research or industry experience

  • You have either a strong machine-learning research record or significant experience building large-scale machine-learning systems

  • You have trained and evaluated language models or built agentic systems

  • You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable owning technically ambiguous problems

  • You are curious about how legal work actually gets done and enjoy working with domain experts

Particularly relevant experience

Any of the following would be valuable, but we do not expect candidates to have all of them:

  • LLM post-training, fine-tuning, or reinforcement learning experience

  • Data curation, synthetic data, or human-in-the-loop data generation pipelines

  • Evaluation harnesses and benchmark development

  • Distributed training, inference, or experiment infrastructure

  • Publications, open-source contributions, or deployed research systems

  • Legal AI or another expert-intensive application domain

Logistics

At Funding Circle, we have the restless energy of a fintech start-up with the stability of a public company. It’s a unique mix that gives Circlers the autonomy to take ownership and the scale to make an impact that truly counts.

We’re a high-performing team that chooses to lift each other up. We challenge, we champion, and we have each other’s backs - because we know that when we stand together, we move faster and build better.

The impact is real: Last year alone, the businesses on our platform generated £7.2bn for the UK economy 📈 Come and join a mission that matters!

[Read our Impact Report] | [See our Trustpilot]

The role ⚡

📍 London (Hybrid) | 🤝 1 day in the office | 💰 Competitive Salary + Benefits

We're looking for a Copywriter to join our Brand team for three days a week.

You'll take ownership of much of our campaign copywriting, reviewing, refining and sharpening copy so it's clear, persuasive and unmistakably Funding Circle. You'll work across brand and product campaigns targeting small businesses, on channels including email, web, digital, print, direct, audio, and organic social.

You'll need to be a self-starter who's comfortable working with a range of stakeholders, giving and receiving feedback, and turning things around quickly. You'll pick up our tone of voice as if it's your own and know instinctively when copy reads right and when it needs another pass.

  • Producing highly converting product copy and content for the website and cross-channel campaigns, working closely with the brand and design teams

We back you to build an incredible career and by joining us, you'll be part of one of The Sunday Times Best Companies to Work For 2026! As a flexible-first employer, we use a "best of both" approach. We also have award-winning parental leave policies. We're here to support you through the big life moments, from fertility treatments to new additions to the family.

Ready to join a mission that matters? We’d love to chat!

title: Front End Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Seamflow

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are:

  • Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

  • $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

  • Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role

A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.

You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for

We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.

What we're actually screening for:

  • You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.

  • You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.

  • You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.

  • You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.

  • You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.

Signals we like, none of them required:

design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.

This is probably not for you if

  • You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

  • You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get

  • Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

  • Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

  • Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

  • Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

  • A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Frontend Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

 

Role

As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets.

  • Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets.

  • Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications.

  • Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows.

  • Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices.

  • Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies.

  • Deep understanding of frontend architecture, state management, browser APIs, and performance.

  • Experience building highly interactive products such as chat, collaboration, productivity, document editing, calendars, or workspaces.

  • Experience with real-time systems, WebSockets, streaming APIs, or collaborative interfaces.

  • Strong product and UI judgment with attention to interaction details.

  • Able to independently own features from technical design through production.

 

Outcomes

  • Users can communicate, write, organise and collaborate seamlessly across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

  • Complex interactions such as group messaging, editing, scheduling and collaboration feel fast and reliable.

  • AI capabilities are integrated naturally into product workflows rather than added as separate chatbot experiences.

  • Frontend architecture remains fast, maintainable and reusable as ActAI expands into new applications and workflows.

 

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript

  • React.js / Next.js

  • HTML / CSS

  • WebSockets / streaming APIs

  • Node.js

  • REST / GraphQL APIs

 

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world-class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high-quality work and learning.

Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment and execute independently. Our goal is to put in the hands of our users a truly magical product.

 

Interview Process

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us and help bring practical AI benefits to billions of users globally.

title: Full Stack Engineer
descriptionHtml:
We are a growing SaaS start-up with an international team, operating on the intersection between two of the world's most fascinating industries - global shipping and global travel.

Over 90% of global trade depends on ships, and the shipping industry depends on the 2 million seafarers who operate them. What most people don't know is there's a complex, mission-critical travel operation going on 24/7 to bring seafarers to the ships where they're needed, when they're needed. That's called crew logistics, and without it, global trade wouldn't function.

But it's an operation often built on manual processes and legacy systems, meaning high-stress for operators, an unreliable experience for seafarers, and poor outcomes for the industry. That is until Tilla enters the scene.

Backed by strong investor support, with more than 10,000 crew changes executed in the platform each year across over 600 vessels globally, our platform is a game changer in crew logistics, streamlining collaboration between operators and seafarers, making crew operations more humane, efficient, and cost-effective.

Join us on the next chapter of our growth journey and tackle this overlooked yet critical global challenge: every crew change, optimized and digital.

Your mission

Build and maintain the Travel services that get seafarers onto the right flights, shipping well-tested features across our TypeScript stack as part of the Travel team. You'll start by taking pressure off the team by solving bugs, serving customer requests and leading investigations, and progress into owning Travel services of your own.

✈️ Keeping travel operations dependable / by resolving bugs and customer requests quickly and properly

  • Investigating and fixing bugs across the Travel services, reproducing each scenario before changing any code

  • Handling day-to-day technical requests from customers and colleagues, and explaining what went wrong in plain terms

  • Adding logging and metrics to what you build, and following runbooks when alerts fire

🧭 Unlocking the product roadmap / by shipping well-defined features end to end

  • Building features across the frontend (React, Next.js) and backend (NestJS, GraphQL, Prisma) in Linear sprints

  • Breaking work into clear steps, surfacing assumptions early, getting feedback on technical decisions and keeping progress and blockers visible

  • Writing unit and integration tests, and acting on code review feedback

📈 Building depth in a sensitive domain / by growing into ownership of Travel services

  • Learning how flight bookings, fares and travel aggregation work, and how they connect to crew changes

  • Taking ownership of a Travel service module over time, including its uptime, bug rates and resolution times

  • Sharing what you learn through clear pull request descriptions and team documentation


You should have

  • Experience: early-career professional experience as a software engineer, building web applications across both frontend and backend.

  • Experience: working knowledge of TypeScript and React, and some exposure to Node.js backends. Familiarity with any of Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, Prisma, Apollo Client, React Query, ShadCN, AWS (Lambda, SQS, RDS, ECS), Jest or Playwright is useful; we don't expect all of it.

  • Experience: exposure to GDS systems (like Amadeus) or travel aggregator platforms is a plus.

  • A high degree of ownership: you take a task from ticket to production and see it through.

  • Sound engineering fundamentals: readable code, sensible tests, and systematic debugging.

  • Technical depth and curiosity: you want to understand how the wider system works, not only the part in front of you.

  • A genuine interest in travel and flight booking, and a willingness to learn the industry in depth.

  • The ability to explain technical issues simply to customers and non-technical colleagues.

  • Clear, proactive communication about progress, risks and blockers.

  • A collaborative approach: you work well with other engineers, ask for help when it's the quicker route, and act on feedback.

  • Experience or interest in early-stage or growth-stage startups.

  • Fluency in English. Other languages are a plus.

  • Based in EMEA or LATAM, with good working-hours overlap with the rest of the Travel team.

Why Join Us?

  • Tackle a unique industry challenge with global impact

  • Be part of an international, mission-oriented, supportive and fun team

  • Do your best work, with leading-edge AI tools for all team members

  • Benefit from support and budget for your learning and development

We believe that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success at Tilla. We make hiring decisions based on your experience and skills. Therefore, we welcome applications from all members of society, regardless of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief.

descriptionHtml:
About Voodoo

Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000 people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. Our games and apps have passed 7 billion downloads and reach 200 million+ active users every month, making Voodoo the #3 mobile publisher worldwide in downloads, after Google and Meta. We were backed by Goldman Sachs, Tencent and GBL along the way.

Team

Our Gaming team is made up of hybrid-casual, casual, and mid-core experts. Our 'Core' games team supports internal and external studios worldwide in creating, developing, and launching new hit games, whilst our 'Live' games team focuses on delivering higher engagement on our existing and successful games.

Joining our Live games team means collaborating with gaming industry experts on globally renowned, enduring games while embracing exciting new entrepreneurial ventures. With over seven billion downloads worldwide and a portfolio of more than 10 resilient hybrid games generating more than $20m per year, we are the world's largest and most successful hybrid publisher.

You will be joining one of our Live Studios, working on Paper.io2.

Role

Paper Party is the multiplayer mode of Paper.io 2. We are looking for a dedicated Game Designer to improve the modes we already have and create new ones from scratch.

All modes will keep the Paper universe, camera and controls. Beyond that, there is a lot of creative freedom. You will explore new rules, objectives, win conditions, pacing and team setups to create a broad range of fun and replayable multiplayer experiences.

You will:

  • Design and prototype new gameplay modes

  • Improve existing Paper Party modes

  • Define simple, readable rules for one-finger controls

  • Iterate quickly through testing, feedback and playtests

  • Balance accessibility, competition, pacing and replayability

  • Identify weak ideas early and confidently cut or reshape them

  • Work closely with the Paper.io 2 team to turn concepts into playable experiences

  • Document your designs clearly

  • Fine-tune modes directly in Unity whenever possible

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys moving quickly from an idea to a playable prototype, testing it and improving it.

Profile

  • 5+ years of experience in mobile F2P games, designing new games, gameplay modes or prototypes from scratch

  • Experience shipping player-facing content, ideally in mobile games

  • A strong understanding of multiplayer and competitive gameplay

  • A good sense of pacing, clarity and player motivation

  • A pragmatic and iterative approach: prototype, test, cut and retry

  • The ability to work independently and take full ownership

  • Strong English communication and collaboration skills

  • AI-first mindset: Comfortable using AI daily and building custom agents or reusable automations to speed up your work

Nice to have

  • Strong Unity experience

  • Experience with mobile controls, multiplayer or party games

  • Experience working on live games or live content

title: General Secretary Associate intern
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. title: GNC Engineer H/F
descriptionHtml:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

The GNC team is growing across Paris and Kyiv. As one of our early GNC engineers, you'll help shape the architecture of our autonomous systems from the earliest design studies through flight testing and final acceptance. We work in short iterations, with a strong culture of experimentation and field validation. Our engineers regularly work alongside operators and end users, ensuring that every algorithm is designed for real operational conditions: not just simulation.

Role & Mission

As a GNC Engineer, you will develop the guidance, navigation, and control capabilities that enable our autonomous platforms to operate reliably in challenging environments. You'll contribute across the entire development lifecycle—from system architecture and flight modelling to live flight testing and operational validation.

We are looking for engineers who enjoy taking ownership of their work, iterating quickly, and seeing their algorithms perform outside the lab.

  • Design, develop, and improve guidance, navigation, and control algorithms for autonomous aerial systems.

  • Develop and maintain flight dynamics and vehicle models.

  • Contribute to system architecture, control strategies, and performance trade-offs from the earliest design phases.

  • Participate in flight-test campaigns and operational demonstrations.

  • Analyze flight data, investigate anomalies, and continuously improve system performance.

  • Work closely with software, AI, systems engineers, test pilots, and operators to validate solutions in real operational conditions.

Requirements

  • Minimum 3 years of professional experience in Guidance, Navigation & Control, flight control, robotics, or autonomous systems.

  • Great systems engineering skills. Prior experience with aerospace V&V processes.

  • Motivation to participate in field testing and work directly on deployed systems.

  • Strong analytical skills, engineering rigor, and ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to Have

  • Programming skills in C++ and Python.

title: GTM Lead Germany
descriptionHtml:
At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.


Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work. Legacy software hasn’t helped, it’s made things slower, more complex, and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change that. Our technology combines Large Language Models with system-level automation to handle real work inside existing hospital tools. No integrations, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding workflows and frees up time for medical staff to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024, are backed by top investors (Index, Frst, Y Combinator, Hexa, Kima Ventures, Better Angle), and we’re just getting started.

 

The future of healthcare isn’t just digital — it’s automated. Come help us build it !

Context

Germany is one of Europe's largest healthcare markets, and its hospitals face the same pressure we solve in France: rising administrative load, staff shortages and revenue lost to incomplete coding.

As Germany GTM Lead, you are our first hire in the country. You will report directly to Paul Lafforgue, CEO and co-founder, and work closely with Chris, our CTO, and the product team in Paris. You will own everything from the first prospecting call to the first signed contracts, shape the local product and build the German team from zero.

  • Location: 2 to 3 months of onboarding in Paris, then based in Germany with regular trips to Paris. Office in Munich or Berlin.

  • Team: none at first. Around 5 people in H1 2027, around 12 by the end of 2027.

Your mission

Take Parallel from zero to a validated, repeatable market in Germany by the end of 2027: 2 to 3 flagship hospitals as paying customers, 2M€ ARR and a local team of around 15.

Outcomes

  • First customers: build the pipeline with Paul, book your own first meetings (your calendar starts empty), sign the first pilots and turn them into paying contracts.

  • German go-to-market: pick the segment to win first (private groups, public or university hospitals), adapt the pitch to the German healthcare context, test our success-based pricing, including in public tenders, and build visibility through networks, trade shows and customer references.

  • Local product: run the feedback loop between German hospitals and the product & tech team, and bring in local medical expert(s) to validate usage

  • German team: hire a team growing from 0 to around 12 across sales, ops, engineers and set up the office.

  • Growth story: report on Germany's progress to the leadership team and investors, and, if we acquire a local company, contribute to due diligence and lead the integration of the acquired team.

Who you are

A builder who wants to open a market, not run one. This job is for you if:

  • You are a native German speaker, with your schooling and career in Germany, and fluent in English, our working language with headquarters.

  • You have 5 to 10 years of experience, including at least 2 years in a quota-carrying B2B sales role.

  • You have lived at least one 0-to-1 experience: you founded a company, joined a startup of fewer than 50 people or launched a new market.

  • You enjoy being on the ground: meeting customers, travelling and opening doors yourself.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and an empty playbook.

  • You are credible with hospital leadership (CEO, CFO, chief medical officer) as well as with physicians.

  • You can convince first hires to join a company that nobody in Germany knows yet.

  • You are open to about 3 months of regular trips to Paris, with a long-term base in Germany.

  • Bonus: you know the German healthcare system, or you have already launched a business.

  • Bonus: you have hired and managed a team, or worked on M&A or the integration of an acquired team.

Our values

  • Play to Win: we are not here just to participate, ship something “good enough”, or enjoy the startup ride. We want to win. That means caring deeply about outcomes, moving fast and being willing to put in the intensity required when it matters.

  • High Trust, High Standards: trust is our default. If you joined us, it's because we believe you can own your scope and make good decisions. We don't want a company built on approvals, control and micromanagement. But trust comes with responsibility. The more freedom we give, the higher the standard we expect.

  • Low Ego, Hands-On: no one at Parallel is above doing the work. Titles, seniority and past achievements don't exempt anyone from getting their hands dirty. Everyone should be willing to step into the arena when needed. Leadership means taking responsibility, not creating distance from execution.

  • Don't Take Yourself Too Seriously: we are extremely serious about our mission. We don't need to be extremely serious about ourselves. Building a company is intense. We want Parallel to remain a place where people enjoy spending time together, laugh, celebrate and bring energy to the people around them. High standards and good vibes are not opposites. We want both.

Hiring process

  1. Screening call (40 min)

  2. Practical case + Q&A with Paul, CEO (video call, 45 min)

  3. Presentation of your written practical case (video call, 1h30)

  4. Business case in Paris (half a day)

Why should you join us?

  • A rare opportunity: open Parallel's first international market as employee #1 in the country, with a direct line to the CEO and the room to build the team, the playbook and the office your way.

  • A product that already works: you start with a live product, around 800 customer references in France and local CTO in Germany ready to adapt it with you.

  • Real-world impact: every hospital you sign gives clinical staff time back from paperwork to improve patient care.

  • Package & perks: competitive salary and meaningful equity, health insurance, top-quality equipment and a public-transport contribution.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

title: Hardware Engineer, FPGA
descriptionHtml:
Normal Computing | Build with Us

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

The Role

Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. Your scope spans the entire FPGA lifecycle: selecting hardware platforms, implementing complex RTL, debugging in the lab, and writing the software that drives it all, working daily with our silicon, EDA, and research teams.

What You Will Own

  • FPGA Platform Ownership: Lead the selection, procurement, and bring-up of FPGA prototyping platforms (e.g., HAPS, VCU118/VPK180-class boards, or custom hardware) for pre-silicon RTL validation and software development.

  • RTL Implementation: Adapt and implement complex ASIC RTL onto FPGA targets, including multi-clock-domain architectures, CDC bridges, and timing closure on dense designs.

  • IP Integration: Integrate in-house designs with third-party and vendor IP; serve as the expert on the AMD/Xilinx ecosystem (Vivado IP Integrator, transceivers, memory controllers).

  • High-Speed Interfaces: Design, implement, and validate high-speed I/O with a focus on PCIe: our accelerators ship as PCIe cards in standard servers.

  • Post-Silicon Validation: Build FPGA-based "tester" designs for silicon bring-up, device characterization, and automated test environments.

  • Hardware-Software Stack: Develop the software layer around the hardware: Python/C++ hardware abstraction, register-map generation, and automated build and regression flows.

  • Lab Debug: Root-cause complex timing and functional issues in real time using ILA/Vivado Analyzer, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and BER/eye-diagram characterization of high-speed links.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • Proven industry experience taking FPGA designs from RTL through timing closure to validated hardware, ideally in an ASIC prototyping, emulation, or high-growth hardware environment.

  • Expert-level SystemVerilog and/or VHDL for synthesis, with deep proficiency in Xilinx Vivado (synthesis, place & route, timing closure, IP catalog).

  • Hands-on experience implementing and debugging PCIe, plus AXI/AHB, SPI, UART, JTAG, and other common interfaces.

  • Strong Python for automation, test, and build tooling.

  • Strong board-level bring-up and lab debugging skills on real hardware.

  • Startup mindset: you work independently, pivot quickly, and run at ambiguous problems that span hardware, software, and physics.

Bonus Points

  • Verification frameworks like Cocotb or UVM

  • Experience deploying ML models to FPGAs (hls4ml, FINN, or custom NN-to-RTL flows), or building real-time, sub-microsecond signal processing pipelines.

  • Mixed-signal ASIC exposure: digital front-ends, ADC/DAC interfaces, or analog compute.

  • SERDES tuning and signal integrity fundamentals.

  • CI/CD for hardware (GitLab CI, Docker-based build and test).

title: Head of Product
descriptionHtml:
Head of Product

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: Full-time (40 hours/week)

Location: Delft, the Netherlands (hybrid
Report to: CEO

About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced on-board UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers that are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members have a background in different fields such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub located on the TU Delft campus in the faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.

Your role

As Head of Product, you own our product hands-on. You are the bridge between what the market and our operators need and what we build, turning field feedback and market insight into a clear roadmap and products people actually want to use. You own how our capabilities become real products: how they are shaped, packaged, priced, taken to market, and adopted by the people who use them in the field.

This is a hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves role, not a purely strategic one. You set the product’s direction together with the founders, and you do the work to make it happen: talking to users, writing requirements, prioritizing the backlog, and working day-to-day with engineering to ship. You bring structure to how we do product without turning it into bureaucracy.

You will work closely with the founders, engineering, and commercial. The company strategy is set with the founders; your job is to own the product within it and make it succeed.

Your responsibilities will include

• Product strategy & roadmap. Owning the product roadmap and prioritization, and keeping the product direction aligned with the company strategy as the market and the technology evolve.

• Market-to-technical bridge. Translating operator needs, market signals, and partner requirements into clear, well-scoped work for engineering, and translating technical capability back into value the market understands.

• Hands-on product delivery. Writing requirements, shaping features, prioritizing the backlog, and working day-to-day with engineering to get things shipped and validated.

• Product portfolio. Helping shape how our capabilities in detection, navigation, interception, and beyond fit together as a modular, scalable line-up rather than isolated tools.

• User experience & adoption. Owning how usable our products are for end users: ease of use, onboarding, training, documentation, and the adoption path from first deployment to routine operational use.

• Pricing & business model. Contributing to pricing, packaging, and business models across the product line-up, and owning the product side of the classic marketing mix (the 4Ps).

• Go-to-market. Partnering with commercial and business development on go-to-market for each capability, from positioning and narrative to capability briefs and demos.

• Market intelligence. Keeping an eye on the market: trends, competitors, adjacent opportunities, and where the next product bets should be.

• Regulatory & compliance awareness. Given the defence context, factoring export control, procurement, and relevant standards into product decisions, working with the right internal and external stakeholders.

• Lightweight product practices. Bringing just enough structure, process, and documentation to make product work repeatable, suited to a fast-moving deep-tech company.

What you will deliver in your first year

• A clear, documented product roadmap, aligned with the founders and understood across the company.

• A working feedback loop that turns field and operational insight into product decisions.

• Well-scoped, prioritized work flowing to engineering, with product shipped and validated with users.

• Input into pricing and business-model choices for the core product lines.

• A joint go-to-market plan with commercial for at least one capability, taken through to execution.

• Measurable improvement in product adoption and usability through better onboarding, documentation, and training for operators and partners.

• A working market map that informs the next set of product bets.

What we expect from you

• 5+ years in product management, with a track record of owning a product’s roadmap and shipping it in a technical product environment.

• Experience in a startup or scale-up environment: comfortable with ambiguity, limited resources, and wearing several hats.

• A strong bridge-builder: you connect customers and market reality to engineering, and you are comfortable in deeply technical conversations without being the engineer yourself.

• A genuinely hands-on mindset: you want to talk to users, write requirements, and work day-to-day with engineering, not only set direction from a distance.

• Exposure to pricing, packaging, and business-model decisions (the product side of the 4Ps).

• Experience working with commercial teams on go-to-market.

• A user-obsessed attitude: you care about adoption, usability, training, and documentation, not only features.

• The ability to read a market, spot trends, and turn them into concrete product opportunities.

• Strong communication and stakeholder skills, from the field and the shop floor to founders, partners, and government stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Domain experience in defence, drones/UAV, aerospace, or other dual-use or high-stakes technology. A real plus, but not a must.

• Experience navigating regulated environments and their impact on product, such as export control, procurement, certification, or standards.

• Experience as an early or first dedicated product hire, setting up lightweight product practices from scratch.

We know this exact combination is rare. If you have a strong track record of building products that reached real users, and the hands-on drive and judgment to navigate the rest, we want to talk.

What we offer

• The chance to own the product of a deep-tech defence company from an early stage, working directly with the founders.

• Equity participation. We want the people building the company to share in it.

• Competitive compensation.

• 25 vacation days per year.

• Reimbursed travel expenses and company laptop.

• (Really) flexible working hours, with a hybrid setup around our Delft office.

• Working in an international, world-class team of engineers and entrepreneurs solving real-life problems with technology that matters.

• Real ownership, fast iteration, and tight feedback loops, and the chance to see what you build deployed in environments where it genuinely counts.

The application procedure

• If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself. This can be a resume, LinkedIn, or other source, as long as we get a clear picture of your background and track record.

• We'll get back to you as soon as possible. If we see a potential fit, we'll set up an initial conversation, followed by deeper sessions with the founders and the team where we work through real product scenarios together.

• If at this point we feel you are the person we are looking for, we'll discuss the specifics.

• Welcome to the team!

title: Head of Product (Flex)
descriptionHtml:
Head of Product 

  • Location: London (Hybrid Office - 3+ days per week)

  • Salary: £112,000 - £140,000

  • Team: Product (Flex)

  • Level: HoD

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

As Head of Product for Flex, you own the vision, strategy and commercial success of our residential VPP platform globally. You lead a product organisation of Product Managers embedded across our device integration, optimisation, monetisation and SaaS platform teams, and you sit on the Flex Leadership team alongside our Head of Engineering, jointly accountable for the performance of the whole Flex business. Specifically, you will:

  • Set and own the global product strategy for Flex, translating Kaluza's company-level strategy into a roadmap spanning device integrations, multi-asset optimisation (EV, battery, solar, HEMS), monetisation and market access, and self-serve SaaS capabilities.

  • Build and lead a high-performing product organisation - hiring, developing and retaining Product Managers of all levels, and identifying and growing the next generation of product leaders within Flex.

  • Make the trade-off calls that matter: balance the needs of our two core client segments - energy retailers and device OEMs - defaulting to retailer priorities where they conflict, in line with Flex's strategy, while protecting the long-term health of the platform.

  • Partner closely with the Head of Engineering and our Commercial and Partnerships teams to align product, technical and commercial strategy, and to make resourcing and investment decisions across Flex's product and engineering teams.

  • Define annual goals and OKRs for Flex, aligned to Kaluza's company strategy, and hold your organisation accountable for delivering measurable commercial and platform-quality outcomes.

  • Be the client-facing expert for Flex product: lead demos and pitches for prospective retailer and OEM clients, contribute to proposals and pricing, and represent Flex's product practice at Kaluza-wide and industry forums.

  • Own the long-term roadmap narrative - kept current, accessible, and able to be told confidently to prospects and clients two years out - as well as internally to engineering, design, partnerships and commercial teams.

  • Build and maintain your network with Product, Partnership, Engineering and Commercial leaders across Kaluza, ensuring insight from Flex feeds into - and benefits from - the wider Kaluza product strategy.

  • Champion product craft and ways of working across Flex, raising the bar for discovery, prioritisation and measurable impact, in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment where judgement on trade-offs matters as much as vision.

What you’ll bring 

Ideally you’ll have/be

  • Be a proven, experienced product leader with a track record of building, leading and developing product teams and people managers, not just individual contributors.

  • Be a seasoned expert in product strategy and execution across the full product lifecycle, with a track record of translating ambiguous, complex problems into a clear strategy and roadmap.

  • Have strong commercial instincts - comfortable owning pricing input, business cases and ROI, and able to demonstrate commercial impact and business growth through your teams.

  • Be an excellent communicator, able to present complex, ambiguous problems clearly and persuasively to technical and non-technical audiences, from engineers to clients to Kaluza's leadership team.

  • Have deep experience with, or a genuine ability to quickly get up to speed in, complex multi-sided B2B / B2B2C technology platforms - direct experience in energy, DER orchestration, IoT device platforms or smart devices is a strong plus.

  • Be comfortable operating with high ambiguity, making the call yourself where appropriate and knowing when to escalate, in a fast-paced and frequently changing environment.

  • Have a track record of fostering a strong product culture and coaching others - including peers without being their formal manager - to raise the standard of product work around them.

  • Be data-driven in how you measure impact, and able to hold yourself and your teams accountable to outcomes, not just outputs.

What will set you apart 

  • Experience in energy trading, national and regional flexibility markets, or other VPP monetisation opportunity spaces (e.g. balancing markets, capacity markets, wholesale/imbalance trading, ancillary services).

  • Direct experience with VPPs, EV/battery smart charging, HEMS, or residential demand-flexibility products.

  • Familiarity with UK and/or international energy market mechanics (e.g. BSC, NEM, market settlement, DER integration standards).

  • Experience selling or supporting the sale of platform/SaaS propositions to enterprise clients.

Where you'll work
We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Head of Talent Acquisition
descriptionHtml:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store.

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 7 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko.

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US.

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us!

🧲 Our Talent Team

At Joko, hiring has been a founding obsession since day one. Our founders have always been convinced that markets aren't cracked with headcount — they're cracked with talent density. That bet has worked: we've grown to 6 million users and become one of France's most recognized shopping apps with just 30 people in the early years, and we've kept the same bar as we've scaled past 100.

The Talent team exists because we believe talent is the single biggest asset of a company, and that identifying, attracting, and closing the best profiles is a craft worth investing in seriously. We are constantly experimenting with state-of-the-art techniques, tools, and processes to find the people who will build the future of shopping with us.

Today, the Talent team sits within the broader People function, which also covers People Ops, People Business Partnering, and Workplace across France, Spain, and our growing international footprint into the US. We are a team with a big scope and rare ownership per person, and we move fast.

✨ Why this role is special

Recruiting is Joko's #1 company objective — because talent unlocks everything else — which makes this one of the most strategic seats in the company. Three things make it genuinely rare:

  • The team is exceptionally involved in hiring. From ICs to managers to founders, recruiting is treated as a first-class responsibility, not something delegated to TA. You will work with hiring partners who actually show up, give sharp feedback, and care about the bar as much as you do.

  • You will have the tools, and the budget, to be on the frontier. We already work with a modern stack (Ashby, Claude, Claap, and more), and we keep investing to stay among the most performant and modern TA setups out there. You will not be fighting for basic tooling, you will be deciding what comes next.

  • You will live a genuinely unique scale moment. Growing from 100+ people today to 200+ within 18 months, with a real international component (France, Spain, US, and more to come) is the kind of stretch many TA leaders don’t often get to experience. You get to do it here, with a company that has already proven it can build a recognized product with a fraction of the usual headcount.

To be concrete about what this looks like in practice: in year one, the job is to build the team — sourcing, hiring, and coaching the TAMs who will power Joko's growth. The AI strategy, international employer brand, and long-term function design are the horizon you are building toward. They are real, and you will own them fully. But the foundation comes first, and the foundation is the team.

🎯 What you will do

As Head of Talent Acquisition, your mission is to build and lead the TA function that will take Joko from 100+ people today to 200+ within 18 months, and beyond, with the bar, craft, and intentionality that have defined Joko's talent density since day one. You will report to the VP People and be part of the People leadership team, alongside the Head of People Operations and our Lead People Business Partner. You will partner closely with founders, hiring managers, and the broader People team.

  • Build and own the TA team: The most important thing you will do, especially early on, is hire the recruiters who will hire everyone else. Two Talent Acquisition Managers are already in the team, and four more TAM positions are open today. You will make the case for what else the function needs over time, from sourcing specialization onward, and recruit, coach, and grow the team around you.

  • Define how Joko recruits: Inbound, outbound, RPO management, agency relationships, tooling (Ashby), and process are all yours. You will set the standards, not just execute against them — including upskilling hiring managers so the bar is applied consistently across every panel.

  • Recruit senior and critical roles yourself: You will stay close to the hardest hires. You know when to delegate and when to own the desk.

  • Build a global AI strategy for recruiting: The way recruiting is done is changing drastically with AI. You will define and roll out Joko's AI strategy for TA: which parts of the funnel to automate, which tools to deploy, how to keep human judgment where it matters most, and how to turn AI into a real competitive advantage in how we source, screen, and close. You will own this end to end.

  • Drive an international employer brand: We are not well known enough yet, and that is costing us. You will build an employer brand strategy that reflects who we actually are, starting in France, scaling very soon to Spain, and preparing for the US and other markets.

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: You have stood up a TA function before, or rebuilt one, and you have also worked somewhere with best-in-class standards. You can operate in both 0-to-1 mode and best-in-class mode, and you know when to switch. The strongest candidate may not have done "just" Talent — a track record that spans ops, sales, consulting, or building things beyond recruiting is a real asset here.

  • Coaching mindset: You know how to develop the resourcefulness and drive of the people you manage. You see growing recruiters as part of the job, not a tax on it.

  • High-bar mindset: Joko's culture is built on talent density. Our hiring managers are involved, exacting, and not afraid to pass on a 90% candidate. You find that energizing, not frustrating.

  • Ops-oriented and performance-driven: You think in systems, not one-offs. You instrument the funnel, care about the numbers, and build process that holds up as the team scales.

  • Strong sense of craft in TA: You know the difference between a recruiter who has relied on inbound for years and one who genuinely knows how to source. You’ve done both, and you know which approach each situation calls for.

  • Analytical skills: You reason with data — funnel metrics, conversion rates, capacity plans — and you use it to drive decisions, not to decorate slides.

  • Attention to detail: You know candidates judge us on every touchpoint — an outreach message, a scorecard, an offer letter — and you hold the bar on all of them.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. You take ownership without being asked, you welcome feedback, and you go the extra mile by default.

  • Curious and experimental about AI: You don't claim to have it all figured out, the field moves too fast for that. But you have hands-on experience deploying AI tools into a TA function, you have strong opinions formed from real attempts (and real failures), and you genuinely enjoy figuring out what works.

  • International scope: Paris, Barcelona, New York, our footprint is growing. You are comfortable recruiting across geographies and building an Employee Value Proposition that resonates in more than one market.

  • Location: Based in Paris.

  • Education: No specific requirement. Track record matters more than credentials.

  • Languages: You are fluent in French and English (our working language). Spanish is a plus.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Compensation: €79K – €114K • Offers Equity

title: Head of VIP, Influencers & PR
descriptionHtml:
About the Role:

Reporting into the Brand Marketing Director, we’re looking for a Head of VIP, Influencers & PR to build TALA’s profile, cultural relevance and desirability through the people, partnerships, moments and conversations that matter.

You’ll lead the strategy across VIP partnerships, Influencers, Ambassadors, Pro, PR, gifting and events, turning TALA into a brand that people see, talk about and want to be part of.

You’ll know and understand that the fastest way to build awareness is to put TALA in the right hands, in the right places, with the right people.

The successful candidate will bring a serious black book of relevant VIPs from celebrities and musicians to stylists, athletes, creators and cultural tastemakers and know how to build genuine relationships with them.

You’ll be responsible for creating the moments that make TALA feel bigger, more culturally relevant and impossible to ignore.

Tasks

What You’ll Own

VIP & Cultural Partnerships

  • Build and own TALA’s VIP strategy, identifying the people who can meaningfully increase awareness, desirability and cultural relevance.
  • Develop relationships with celebrities, musicians, stylists, athletes, tastemakers and influential cultural figures.
  • Bring a strong existing network and continually build TALA’s VIP black book.
  • Create strategic partnerships that go beyond gifting from organic product placement to collaborations, appearances and brand moments.
  • Ensure TALA is consistently seen on the right people, in the right places and at the right cultural moments.

Ambassador & Pro Programmes

  • Own the strategy, vision and evolution of TALA’s Ambassador and Pro programmes.
  • Define the role these programmes play within TALA’s broader brand and awareness strategy, including who we want to attract, why they matter and what we want them to deliver.
  • Establish the programme proposition, structure, tiers, criteria and long-term growth strategy.
  • Together with the team, build a best-in-class network of ambassadors and professional athletes who genuinely align with TALA and can become powerful advocates for the brand.
  • Set the strategic direction for recruitment, relationship development, activation and retention, with the team responsible for day-to-day programme management and execution.
  • Continuously assess and evolve the programmes based on KPIs including brand impact, reach, engagement and commercial contribution.

Influencer

  • Own the overall influencer strategy, defining how influencer partnerships drive awareness, cultural relevance, desirability and growth.
  • Set the direction for the talent TALA works with, from high-profile creators and cultural tastemakers to emerging talent and community voices.
  • Identify opportunities to move beyond traditional influencer activity into cultural partnerships, organic product placement and high-impact moments.
  • Ensure influencer strategy is integrated with VIP, Ambassador, Pro, PR, gifting, social and campaign activity.
  • Set clear KPIs and continuously evolve the strategy based on performance and cultural opportunity.

Gifting

  • Own the strategic direction for TALA gifting, transforming it from a reactive PR function into a significant awareness and brand-building engine.
  • Together with the team, define who TALA should be gifting, when, why and what we want gifting to achieve.
  • Oversee the strategy for key product launches, cultural moments, VIP gifting, stylist seeding and wider brand moments.
  • Lead the team in developing, signing off and executing gifting programmes, ensuring activity ladders back to wider brand and campaign priorities.

PR

  • Together with the Brand Marketing Director own the overall PR strategy and communications agenda for TALA.
  • Define the role of PR within the wider brand strategy and how it will contribute to building fame, credibility and awareness.
  • Set the annual PR strategy, priorities, narratives and key cultural moments, working closely with Brand Marketing, Social, Influencer and Product.
  • Brief the PR agency to establish the types of stories TALA should be known for and proactively identify opportunities to create news rather than simply respond to it.
  • Ensure the PR team and agency has a clear roadmap and empower them to execute against it.

Events & Experiences

  • Own the TALA events and experiences strategy, defining how physical brand experiences can drive awareness, desirability, community and growth.
  • Set the annual events strategy, including the role of VIP events, consumer experiences, cultural moments, product launches, retail activations and larger-scale brand moments.
  • Define what makes a TALA experience distinctive and ensure every activation is rooted in the brand and designed to generate impact beyond the room.
  • Identify and feed into the events team opportunities for TALA to create culturally relevant moments that can extend into PR, social and organic conversation.
  • Oversee the brief and objectives for key events, with the team responsible for planning and delivering the experience.
  • Oversee the evaluation of the effectiveness of events against awareness, reach, brand impact and commercial objectives, continually evolving the approach.

Requirements

About You

We’re looking for someone who is highly connected, culturally switched-on and relentlessly ambitious.

You will likely have:

  • Significant experience across VIP, celebrity, influencers, PR and events within fashion, beauty, lifestyle or a culturally relevant consumer brand.
  • A strong existing network of VIPs, stylists, agents, managers, media and cultural tastemakers.
  • A proven ability to build authentic relationships with high-profile talent.
  • Experience creating campaigns and moments that generate significant awareness and organic conversation.
  • Strong commercial and strategic thinking, understanding that awareness must ultimately contribute to brand and business growth.
  • A strong understanding of culture, fashion, music, TV, sport, entertainment and what makes people talk.
  • An instinct for what feels cool, relevant and TALA.
  • Exceptional relationship-building and negotiation skills.
  • The confidence to challenge the status quo and create ideas that haven't been done before.
  • A highly proactive, entrepreneurial approach, you’ll spot opportunities rather than wait for a brief.
  • The ability to operate at both strategic and executional level, from defining the annual VIP strategy to picking up the phone to a stylist.

What Success Looks Like

You’ll know you’re succeeding when:

  • TALA is increasingly seen on the right people.
  • We have a strong and growing network of A-list and culturally relevant VIPs who genuinely want to wear and engage with TALA.
  • TALA becomes a brand that celebrities, stylists and cultural tastemakers actively want to be associated with.
  • Our Ambassador and Pro programmes become recognised as some of the most exciting programmes in the category.
  • Gifting creates genuine organic reach, conversation and product desire.
  • Our events become moments people want to attend and talk about.
  • TALA earns more high-quality PR and cultural coverage.
  • We create moments that travel across social, PR and culture, delivering awareness well beyond the original activation.
  • Most importantly, you help move TALA from a brand people discover on social media to a brand people know, recognise and want.

Benefits

What we can offer:

  • 25 days holiday a year plus bank holidays
  • Very generous employee discount after probation period
  • Nominated Friends & Family Discount
  • Clothing allowance spending gift
  • Class Pass or Gym Flex membership
  • Health Shield
  • Enhanced maternity/paternity pay
  • Charity fundraising match of up to £1,000

About us:

TALA is an activewear brand built to actively solve problems without creating new ones for people, the planet, or anyone else. Every collection prioritises functionality and thoughtful design, combining premium fabrics with multi-way versatility and flattering fits that deliver maximum impact with minimal effort. Each piece is crafted with attention to detail, ensuring women can look and feel their best with ease.

When founder Grace Beverley shifted from fast fashion to more sustainable options in her everyday clothing, she found a host of responsibly made options in every category other than activewear. Founding TALA in 2019, the proud female-led brand is on a mission to make consciously made active and off-duty styles accessible and inclusive without sacrificing performance or fit.

Read about TALA's people, purpose and product work here.
